context: A uni intern interviews a manager about brand storytelling
purpose: Teach: 修士/勧誘/創刊/劣化/書士/ウェブログ/意味合い/度合い

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: お忙しいところすみません。修士論文のために、御社のブランド戦略について伺いたくて。
lines.en: Sorry to bother you. I'd like to ask about your company's brand strategy for my master's thesis.
lines.style: Polite student opening with humble nervous tone

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: どうぞどうぞ。実は私、入社直後に社内報の創刊号に携わったんですよ。
lines.en: Please, go ahead. Actually, right after joining I worked on the inaugural issue of our internal newsletter.
lines.style: Warm professional welcome with proud reminiscence

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: へえ、そうなんですか。今はウェブログ形式で発信されてますよね。媒体を変えた意味合いって何でしょう?
lines.en: Oh really? Now it's published as a blog, right? What's the significance of changing the format?
lines.style: Curious follow-up with genuine intellectual interest

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 紙だと情報の劣化が早くて。読者の関心の度合いも、デジタルの方が正確に測れるんです。
lines.en: With paper the information degrades quickly. We can also measure reader interest more accurately digitally.
lines.style: Calm analytical explanation with measured business reasoning

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。ちなみに、学生時代に強引な勧誘とか受けて、広報の仕事に興味を持たれたんですか?
lines.en: I see. By the way, did some pushy recruitment pitch as a student get you interested in PR work?
lines.style: Light teasing question with friendly conversational pivot

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: いえいえ、むしろ逆で。最初は行政書士を目指してたんですよ。法律より物語の方が面白くなっちゃって。
lines.en: No, the opposite actually. At first I was aiming to be an administrative scrivener. Stories ended up more interesting than law.
lines.style: Self-deprecating chuckle revealing unexpected career pivot

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 面白い経歴ですね。最後に一つ、ブランドストーリーで一番大事なものって何だと思われますか?
lines.en: What an interesting background. One last question, what do you think matters most in brand storytelling?
lines.style: Respectful closing question with thoughtful interviewer cadence

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 嘘をつかないこと。それに尽きます。論文、頑張ってくださいね。
lines.en: Not lying. That's everything. Good luck with your thesis.
lines.style: Firm sincere conclusion with kind parting encouragement
